fences.title: Bunny is the healthy-path portrait accelerator
fences.decision: Healthy browser tabs load content-addressed portrait and requested labelled-card bytes directly from Bunny; one failed real-image probe selects the canonical first-party fallback for that tab. The first-party Worker uses one server-side portrait-storage adapter and treats authenticated Storage and the public CDN as distinct regional views of the same immutable key; only failure of every configured view is missing. Website Ops records split-view success distinctly and exposes operator-triggered, bounded rechecks for verdicts older than 30 days.
fences.reason: Direct Bunny delivery avoids charging every healthy portrait or labelled-card read to the Cloudflare Worker budget. A resolver failure on one network is the reason the fallback exists, not evidence that Bunny should be disabled globally. CASP8AP2 proved the inverse black swan: the full image loaded through an American VPN while the Vietnam first-party Storage read returned 404, so neither one successful region nor one failed provider view establishes global object truth.
fences.change_control: Retiring or replacing Bunny, changing server-side read order, or adding a provider-specific read path requires an explicit architecture migration that updates this registry, the delivery runbook, the single storage adapter, source policy, production and staging configuration, behavioral tests, and deploy guard in one reviewed change. Regional incidents must preserve separate evidence for client DNS, first-party delivery, authenticated Storage, and CDN replica visibility.

fences.title: Gene discovery is eligibility-gated and range-stable
fences.decision: Complete canonical profiles are indexable through one published-catalog predicate, while aliases redirect, incomplete profiles remain noindex, unknown symbols return 404, and the crawlable archive uses frozen self-locating prefix ranges rather than numeric pages. Homepage discovery reuses the existing non-visual description instead of adding visible archive controls; accessibility skip links are clipped until focused. Decorative printed selector alternatives are CSS-rendered ink rather than peer DOM facts, while their noninteractive fields name the resolved molecular value and mapped character result. Model-training crawlers are blocked before Worker execution while AI search and user-directed retrieval agents remain allowed.
fences.reason: Agents need explicit card mappings and a link path they can choose from a known symbol, but that crawler frontier must not become perfunctory chrome that breaks the human card-gallery immersion or let model-training crawlers exhaust the shared Worker allowance. Frozen ranges provide the path without guessing, the shared eligibility gate prevents arbitrary application shells or incomplete cards from becoming an unbounded search corpus, and purpose-specific crawler policy preserves AI search without paying for training ingestion.
fences.change_control: Gene response headers, HTML metadata, homepage discovery placement, archive membership, sitemap membership, llms.txt, renderer semantics, crawler WAF policy, robots.txt, deploy reconciliation, tests, instructions, and runbook must change atomically. Range boundaries may change only through an explicit biological-inventory migration; routine catalog publications must never rebalance them. Do not add the archive to the immersive Archive/Clans switcher, expose feed skip links at rest, represent decorative selector ink as interactive controls or peer facts, or replace the purpose-specific crawler split with a blanket AI-bot block.

fences.title: Queue wakeups follow durable due times
fences.decision: Cloudflare Queue messages wake durable ledger work only when it is runnable; unfinished future work is delayed until the earliest next_attempt_at and is never polled by immediate replacement messages.
fences.reason: A single future retry otherwise creates an ack/read/delete/send feedback loop that consumes the daily Queue allowance without doing work. Short polling caps also spend retry attempts and can dead-letter a message before its durable backoff expires.
fences.change_control: Queue topology, durable status accounting, retry delays, consumer configuration, behavioral tests, instructions, and the runbook must change atomically. Any replacement must prove a bounded number of billable operations while no work is due.

fences.title: The primary Iconoplasm D1 is bounded operational state
fences.decision: The primary D1 stays below an 80% target of its 500,000,000-byte per-database wall by storing immutable profile prose once and moving publish events older than 30 days to a separately bound cold audit D1 after row-level verification.
fences.reason: Duplicated manifestation prose and an unbounded 297,818-row publish ledger filled the database and stopped all writes. The old dashboard compared the database to the unrelated 5 GB account allowance, so it reported roughly 10% usage at the per-database hard limit.
fences.change_control: Large payload placement, read-model columns, append-only ledgers, retention, archive bindings, capacity thresholds, observability, migrations, tests, instructions, runbook, and deploy enforcement must change atomically. Cold history may be removed from the hot database only after verified archival.

fences.title: Fulfillment is one bounded receipt per completed publication, recipient, and gene
fences.decision: A completed generation session has one durable publication identity. Discord delivery waits for each complete publication-recipient-gene group, sends one message with at most ten full-resolution preview images, and links the authoritative gene gallery for the complete result set. The Request inbox mirrors the same durable receipt boundary with a bounded preview mosaic and group-level read acknowledgement.
fences.reason: Request-time button presses are not a meaningful notification boundary. The durable workstation publication is the point where the exact completed images are known. Completion-time or cron-window grouping is still unsafe because it can merge unrelated publications or fragment retries. Discord cannot carry one hundred useful image attachments in one message, and the Worker must keep memory and subrequests bounded.
fences.change_control: Durable publication identity, fulfillment group-size columns, delivery-pending trigger snapshots, group completeness, Discord and Request inbox presentation, group-level read acknowledgement, attachment and memory ceilings, nonce idempotency, reconciliation, workstation payloads, behavioral tests, instructions, and this runbook must change atomically. Never replace the durable publication boundary with timing, row adjacency, or request-time clicks.

fences.title: Iconoplasm is static-first with one dynamic Worker invocation
fences.decision: The Iconoplasm custom hostname is owned directly by the existing stateful Worker, where matching build artifacts are served by Workers Static Assets before Worker execution and dynamic misses enter that Worker exactly once.
fences.reason: On the Free plan, the former wildcard public proxy charged one public and one internal invocation for every request, including more than one hundred static dependencies on a normal page. Asset-first delivery removes static traffic from the Worker quota and direct dynamic routing removes the redundant proxy invocation without changing vote authority or adding a state holder.
fences.change_control: Route ownership, static bundle construction and limits, security headers, rate-limit ownership, stateful bindings, deployment order, tests, instructions, and this runbook must change atomically. A replacement must be selected from current production evidence and prove equal or lower Worker use while preserving complete gene first paint and strongly ordered votes; this fence is not authority by tradition.

fences.title: Anonymous startup and extension hover use the published read plane
fences.decision: Anonymous homepage startup avoids auth, settings, inventory, and admin probes; authenticated startup is gated by a non-authoritative session-presence hint. The visible signed-out archive contains the four fixed published starters INS, RHO, PRL, and CD4; decorative reverse-card continuation is inert markup and never expands the discovery set or triggers reads. Signed-out dossier visits persist across the full 19,023-gene browser-local shelf; an authenticated page session merges at most 200 pending symbols and retains the remainder for later sessions. Extension pages receive a separately versioned scanner artifact capped at 3 MiB with no portrait references. Visible and hovered genes hydrate immutable published card details into a 4 MiB revision-keyed cache. The complete admin-managed shared text blocklist is a separately revisioned KV projection carried by the existing catalog manifest; clients retain the last valid projection and use the packaged list only as first-run or offline fallback.
fences.reason: The shoutout risk is sustained daily request and D1 consumption, while the browser risk is cloning cold portrait metadata into every tab and crossing Chromium's 10 MiB storage quota. Separating the compact matcher from bounded on-demand card detail keeps both public infrastructure work and per-user browser cost proportional to real use. Carrying the tiny shared-term policy in the manifest avoids a second polling path, catalog rebuilds, and divergent packaged default lists.
fences.change_control: Anonymous bootstrap, session-presence semantics, catalog, scanner, card and shared-term publication metadata, public batch projection, extension scanner and shared-term migration, storage budgets, cache invalidation, tests, instructions, and this runbook must change atomically. The readable marker must never carry identity or authority, public shared-term reads must never fall back to D1, term-only revisions must not rebuild the scanner, transient public-read failures must remain retryable, and portrait references must not return to the per-tab scanner map.

fences.title: Iconoplasm public reads stay cold-safe inside the one loud state boundary
fences.decision: Canonical gene first paint uses a publication-owned O(1) D1 identity index with no portrait or vote fields, then uses the current D1 detail ETag for HTML freshness and checks the HTML cache before detail parsing or rendering. All extracted modules remain behind the existing loudly named single state owner.
fences.reason: Disposable Cloudflare isolates make process warmth an invalid correctness assumption. A broad refactor can also accidentally recreate the retired public-proxy topology if the protective filenames and route owner are treated as ordinary names.
fences.change_control: The cold-path order, published route-membership barrier, current-detail ETag authority, protected filenames, topology manifest, deployment order, module naming rules, tests, instructions, runbook, and production workflow must change atomically. Never put mutable portrait or vote state in the route index; add a second Worker, public proxy, or service-binding hop for normal reads; or replace the protective prefix/suffix with a shortened responsibility-only boundary name.

fences.title: Routine gallery publication is dirty-shard-only
fences.decision: Canonical publish events prepare only their owning content-addressed card shards, in steps of at most six shards per Worker invocation, then atomically flip one manifest. Routine cron and voting paths never rebuild the complete catalog.
fences.reason: The fixed gene universe makes a complete-catalog rebuild unrelated to normal vote scope. The former scattered-delta fallback delayed visible votes, consumed avoidable KV operations, and made an exceptional migration mechanism look like ordinary publication.
fences.change_control: Dirty-symbol event windows, stable shard ownership, local insertion/removal/split behavior, one-step scheduled execution, atomic manifest and watermark order, KV budget accounting, bounded operation audits, migration fail-closed errors, naming rules, tests, instructions, and this runbook must change atomically. Never introduce a dirty-count or shard-count threshold that falls back to complete-catalog work.

fences.title: Signed-in account galleries use one canonical portrait artifact
fences.decision: Personal and shared account windows use discovery data only for membership and order, then project every displayed portrait from the exact published card artifact selected by KV_GALLERY_VERSION. The image-only view is a compact projection of that same card VM, not a separate portrait read plane.
fences.reason: The former image-only branch used a separately versioned published-portrait-reference snapshot. Routine dirty-shard publication could advance the card artifact without advancing that snapshot, so logged-in Edge showed old light-purple ZNF25 on the homepage while the same session's gene page showed the current dark-gray canonical.
fences.change_control: Account-window membership, ordering, card-artifact selection, image-only projection, cache keys, behavioral tests, instructions, and both portrait/home runbooks must change together. Never restore discovery-row portrait identity, publishedPortraitRefs, browser-local portrait state, or another independently versioned snapshot as an image-only source. Any replacement must prove a single publication selects the same visible portrait on the signed-in homepage and gene page in one browser session.

fences.title: Daily targets give every gene surname one slot
fences.decision: Automatic GeneGuessr daily selection walks a deterministic without-replacement shuffle-bag of normalized gene surnames and chooses one deterministic representative per surname. Automatic targets cannot repeat inside one complete playable-surname cycle. Manual overrides and recorded availability replacements remain explicit exceptions.
fences.reason: Hashing across the flat protein table makes large families proportionally more likely. The surname-balancing schema and practice selector existed, but daily mode bypassed them and automatically selected SLC22A5, SLC6A8, and SLC12A2 in July 2026.
fences.change_control: The source pool and its cache fingerprint, family grouping, deterministic shuffle-bag, AlphaFold and structure-availability fallback, admin schedule cache version, pre-warm path, request-time path, instructions, runbook, and behavioral tests must change together. Never restore flat-table weighting, independent per-date hashing, or adjacent-row fallback.

fences.title: Recap images require pixel and storage proof
fences.decision: A GeneGuessr recap image is publishable only after the browser proves stable molecule pixels and object storage returns the exact uploaded bytes from the immutable day, UniProt, and renderer identity. Missing images preserve the text recap; repairs edit the recorded Discord message in place. Annual coverage is a resumable reconciliation: bounded preflight and final reads, skip verified objects, group missing days by protein, retain one bitmap at a time, and report success only for 365/365 exact objects.
fences.reason: The July renderer uploaded a uniform dark canvas that Discord displayed as a blank attachment. The August Bunny cutover then accepted an upload response without proving the object existed, so NHP2 posted without an attachment while the admin UI reported success and its startup warning crashed before schedule initialization. B-702 then found only 1 of 365 yearly objects ready and proved the old bulk button had no checkpoint, skip-ready behavior, memory bound, or exact final audit.
fences.change_control: Renderer readiness, object identity, upload success semantics, read-back verification, bounded bulk reconciliation, admin coverage, text-only fallback, posted-message repair, instructions, runbook, and behavioral tests must change together. Never treat attachment presence, a generic 2xx, object metadata, an attempted-upload count, or non-zero byte length as proof that a visible protein will reach Discord.

fences.title: Remote prose checks are explicit, snapshot-bound, and free-Zen-only
fences.decision: Harper grammar may run locally after editor idle, while DeepSeek prose agents run only after an explicit user command against one immutable complete-document snapshot. Remote startup and typing paths read no credential and send no traffic. The sole remote model is deepseek-v4-flash-free on OpenCode Zen, with no paid, Go, or alternate-provider fallback.
fences.reason: Whole-document atomic agents take roughly one to two minutes apiece and duplicate private prose across requests. A live trigger would race edits, flood the provider, worsen Obsidian startup, and send drafts without deliberate consent. A silent fallback could convert expiry of the free preview into unbounded paid use.
fences.change_control: Plugin startup, editor events, run commands, model routing, credential reads, agent granularity, anchor validation, runbook, and behavioral tests must change together. Any replacement must preserve explicit initiation, immutable full-document snapshots, exact one-error agents, and fail-closed cost behavior.
